description: Figure 14 is a single Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase diagram (a pseudo-binary section) calculated for the Fe-12Mn-9Al-1.4C-3Cr-xNb (x = 0–0.05 wt%) system, plotted as Temperature (K) on the vertical axis against Nb content (wt.%) on the horizontal axis. The y-axis carries labelled ticks at 673, 873, 1073, 1273, 1473 and 1673 K; the x-axis runs from 0 to 0.05 wt% Nb in 0.005 wt% steps. A gently rising blue solvus curve separates a large FCC (austenite) field at low temperature from the BCC+FCC region above it, while a flat purple line near 1673 K bounds the Liquid and Liquid+BCC fields at the top. Several coloured horizontal isotherms (tan, purple, green, blue, orange, lavender) partition the lower part of the diagram into narrow multiphase bands, labelled from top to bottom: Liquid, Liquid+BCC, BCC+FCC, BCC+FCC+MC, FCC, FCC+MC, FCC+κ, FCC+κ+MC, BCC+FCC+κ, BCC+FCC+MC+κ, BCC+FCC+κ+M7C3, BCC+MC+κ+M7C3, BCC+MC+κ+M7C3+M23C6 and BCC+MC+κ+M23C6. Black arrows link the narrow low-Nb corner regions to their labels. No numeric temperatures are printed on the isotherm lines, so the phase-boundary temperatures can only be read against the y-axis gridlines. The diagram demonstrates that adding Nb strongly raises the MC (NbC) precipitation temperature while only weakly shifting the liquid-to-solid transformation temperature.

observations.observation: The figure is a single Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase diagram with Temperature (K) on the y-axis (labelled ticks at 673, 873, 1073, 1273, 1473, 1673 K) and Nb content (wt.%) on the x-axis (0 to 0.05, ticked every 0.005).
A continuous blue curve rises from low Nb content (starting around the 1150 K level at 0 wt% Nb) to about the 1573 K level at 0.05 wt% Nb, separating the FCC field below from the BCC+FCC field above.

Phase-field labels printed on the diagram include Liquid, Liquid+BCC, BCC+FCC, BCC+FCC+MC, FCC, FCC+MC, FCC+κ, FCC+κ+MC, BCC+FCC+κ, BCC+FCC+MC+κ, BCC+FCC+κ+M7C3, BCC+MC+κ+M7C3, BCC+MC+κ+M7C3+M23C6 and BCC+MC+κ+M23C6.

The lower part of the diagram is subdivided by several horizontal coloured isotherm lines (tan, purple, green, blue, orange, lavender); these lines carry no printed numeric temperature values, so their temperatures are only readable against the y-axis gridlines.
The caption states the diagram is an equilibrium phase diagram calculated by Thermo-Calc software for the Fe-12Mn-9Al-1.4C-3Cr-xNb (x = 0–0.05) system.
The citing text states the diagram was analysed using Thermo-Calc with the TCFE10 database.
The citing text states that as the Nb content increases from 0 to 0.05 wt%, the precipitation temperature of NbC (drawn as the MC phase) increases from ≈973 to 1573 K.

The citing text states that the Nb content has limited impact on the temperature at which the liquid-to-solid phase transformation occurs, leading to similar constituent phase content in the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.

The citing text states that small changes in Nb content have a significant impact on the formation of the NbC (MC) phase, and that the high formation temperature of NbC allows the particles to pin austenite grain boundaries during the δ-ferrite→γ-austenite transformation.
Black arrows connect the narrow low-Nb-corner phase regions to their printed labels (FCC+κ, FCC+κ+MC, BCC+FCC+κ, BCC+FCC+κ+M7C3, BCC+FCC+MC+κ).
A small triangular pointer/marker icon is present in the bottom-left corner of the plot frame.

subfigures.description: A single Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase diagram: Temperature (K) from 673 to 1673 K versus Nb content (wt.%) from 0 to 0.05, showing a rising blue solvus boundary separating FCC from BCC+FCC, a top purple line bounding Liquid and Liquid+BCC, and multiple horizontal coloured isotherms subdividing the low-temperature region into 14 labelled phase fields (FCC, FCC+MC, FCC+κ, FCC+κ+MC, BCC+MC+κ+M7C3, BCC+MC+κ+M23C6, etc.). No numeric temperatures are printed on the isotherm lines; a small triangular pointer icon sits at the bottom-left corner.
